text:
sara: heads-up: CI alert for ap-south L4 (A10) — p99 token latency jumped ~2.3x after merge 4289. noticed during the canary rollout.
james: saw the alert, digging in. is this the batching heuristic change PR? 4289 was the one that nuked micro-batches right?
kyle: yes PR 4289 changed batch flush timeout + prefilling behavior for smaller seqs. I thought it reduced tail latency though.
ana: @sara can you paste sample trace or perf profile? ci-bot only shows aggregate numbers right now.
sara: putting a quick repro link and flamegraph: https://internal.perf.redwood/graphs/fg-2123456789.svg
sara: quick snippet from the trace:
```
request: seq=32 tokens
selected_kernel: dynamic_chunker_v2
kv_cache_hits: 0 -> evict spike
queue_wait_ms: 24 -> 180
gpu_exec_ms: 6 -> 9
```
james: interesting — queue_wait jump suggests something upstream (network/ingress) or pre-exec batching behavior changed.
kyle: i profiled kernel selector during the repro, looks like selector is preferring dynamic_chunker_v2 on A10 for mid-length sequences now, whereas before it used the legacy small-batch kernel. dynamic_chunker has worse prefetch pattern on A10 memory layout.
sara: that matches perf: flamegraph shows heavy time in device memcpy + kvcache-evict loop.
ana: any noisy neighbor evidence on that host? I/O metrics?
james: checked host metrics: NIC transmit queues show burst at the same time — but only on a subset of pods in the AZ. packet drops ~0.2% but tail effect looks amplified by batching.
ci-bot: CI pipeline 4289-canary failed 3/5 perf checks: p99 tokens above SLO on ap-south-a10 cluster.
kyle: hypothesis: batching heuristic change increased coalescing window -> bigger prefix groups -> KV cache gets warm contention and triggers evictions causing extra memcopies. On A10 that memcopy pattern kills p99.
sara: agree. quick experiment idea: revert batching flush timeout to previous value, or force kernel selector override to prefer legacy_small on A10.
james: i can try a canary override (runtime config) to pin kernel selector back. deploying canary now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: runtime-config-pin-legacy-kernel -> ap-south-l4 (canary) (id: d-2123)
ana: while deploy runs, we should bisect PR 4289 to the specific commit that touched `batching/prefill` and `kernel/selector` heuristics.
kyle: did a quick git bisect locally: the regression appears after commit c6f9b1 that changed `prefill_threshold` math. not entirely sure why kernel selector picks dynamic_chunker though — maybe a downstream weight change.
sara: if canary shows p99 back to baseline we can hold 4289 rollback until we implement a more targeted fix. otherwise plan to revert.
deploy-bot: canary finished: 1/1 hosts updated. Metrics: p99 token latency dropped from 2.3x -> 1.05x (near baseline).
sara: nice. keep canary pinned and roll out to remaining hosts slowly.
james: opened PR to add an A10-specific selector override + test to catch this (PR #4330). also adding a perf regression test in CI that runs a small A10 perf repro (fast microbenchmark) to avoid silent rollouts.
kyle: also adding KV-cache eviction logging when eviction rate > 5% for 1m so we can alert earlier.
ana: good. postmortem notes: root cause likely interaction between batching window increase + kernel selector weight changes leading to suboptimal kernel choice on A10 => KV eviction churn => memcopy + NIC queue amplification.
sara: thanks all. next steps: 1) keep runtime override until PR 4330 merges 2) add CI microbenchmark 3) add eviction alert 4) add e2e perf test for ap-south-a10 cluster. I'll file a rollout blocker if 4330 doesn't land by EOD tomorrow.
james: added blocker issue: https://issues.redwood/infra/5678
kyle: i'll follow up on adding the perf test harness and upload artifacts to the perf bucket.
ana: 👍 keep updates here, call me if we need an urgent revert.
ci-bot: note: will auto-block future canaries of 4289 until PR 4330 is merged.
